notes: Independently examined the semantic sections of all 27 cached READMEs, their public installation statements, fixed-tree SKILL.md paths, root/nearest-license scope, and published-inventory metadata. This was not merely a reread of the collector audit notes.

Accepted counts total 173 and exactly match the 173 published-inventory entries and published_skill_paths; every published path exists in its cached fixed Git tree. The inventory contains 173 unique skill names and 173 unique SHA256 values. This deduplication statement describes recorded inventory evidence and is not a substitute for the root agent full tree-bound byte recheck.

AgriClaw has 34 public skill identities including its separately readable router; templates/python-skill/SKILL.md and templates/r-skill/SKILL.md are correctly excluded. The public router was read directly through its fixed-tree Git blob d52d8877faec5297f55b953a8293722bd6715871.

Aegro README explicitly separates customer/Services public skills from private internal engineering skills. The potentially ambiguous aegro-feedback-dev was read directly through fixed-tree Git blob 0748e748474c897e7d0ff17f501a7adb820fd925: it supports external-customer public-form feedback as well as internal customer-services delivery, prohibits repository/Git operations, and is not a hidden repository-maintenance skill. Count 20 is supported.

Chef router and chef-culinary-inspector were read directly through fixed-tree Git blobs 2d2fbcf175689d7e587395a8eeb39c0988803773 and 7296c8ab8fcd768aa47a9f92ae12d67b56d0f4ab. They implement public cooking-task routing and dish/kitchen review, rather than repository-maintenance templates; count 40 including the router is supported.

UnderAutomation README publishes the ten brand/language plugins and states all repository skill text/examples are MIT while SDKs remain commercial. All ten near-plugin license evidences are separately listed. The ten package identities are meaningful public distributions, not duplicate language copies counted as distinct engines.

Green Claude root and near-skill LICENSE explicitly allocate SKILL.md/rules/documentation to CC BY 4.0 and executable code/scripts to Apache-2.0; this is allocation by content type, not a dual-license choice. Existing accepted wording correctly preserves that distinction. Historical third-party MIT contributions and other source-attribution terms remain exceptions under the license text.

LeafEngines LICENSE explicitly limits MIT to skill integration code; the API is a separately commercial service with a free tier and patent-protected core algorithms. The accepted license and count-one wording already reflects that scope.

Helionyx README separates Apache-2.0 core/skill, CC BY 4.0 data packs and EUPL-1.2/AGPL-3.0 optional solver adapters. Counting one agent skill instead of 22 MCP tools is supported; the summary does not claim validated engineering design or bankable feasibility.

Adamek free founder-checks plugin has four public skill paths; the separately sold defense kit is not present in the counted tree. EarthLegend is the owner-published public plugin distribution generated from LGND source, rather than an unrelated third-party mirror. No README/metadata evidence of a pure mirror being miscounted was found.

Edamam Apache-2.0 covers the skill; README separately says hosted MCP access is governed by Edamam API Terms. This does not change the one-skill count or the source-code license. External software/data-service terms are not covered by repository license labels.
No repository, Git state, candidate installation or candidate execution was changed. Only this review JSON was written in the requested temporary root.
